question: Why do web maps stop at about 85 degrees north and south?
answer: The Mercator formula stretches without limit towards the poles, so the map has to be cut somewhere. Web maps cut at latitude 85.05 degrees, where the projected height equals the projected width of the whole world. That makes the map an exact square, which square map tiles divide neatly.
move: Every neat design hides a boundary someone chose to cut.
reference: Battersby, Finn, Usery and Yamamoto, Implications of Web Mercator and Its Use in Online Mapping, Cartographica, 2014
